subject: Non-reversible path coefficients for DWLS estimator?

messages.author: 52d9b08e7d0d0c15
messages.subject: Non-reversible path coefficients for DWLS estimator?
parts:
Hi there, 

I am currently working on a project where I have the following paths: Z->X, Y->X and Z->Y. Where X is a binomial variable and Y and Z are composite variables. When I change the direction of the final path (ie. Y->Z rather than Z->Y) I have found that this also changes the path estimates for the other two paths. However this seems to only occur when I use a diagonally weighted least squares estimator (as opposed to Maximum Likelihood etc.). It does not make sense to me as to why the path coefficients of Z->X and Y->X would change given a directional change of Z->Y (to Y->Z). Is this just an artifact of the DWLS estimator that I am not fully understanding, or something a little more serious? I have presented my R output using the DWLS estimator below.

Any help at all would be greatly appreciated!! (I would also like to apologize for the armature question).  



> B4610model.1<-'X~Z
+ X~Y
+ Z~Y'
> B4610model.1.fit<-sem(B4610model.1,data=B4610PAnew,estimator="DWLS",ordered="X")
